messages:
support_jay: Hey team — getting an escalation from ACME. Over the last ~45m their embeddings calls to /v1/embeddings are seeing tail latencies (p95/p99) spike and a handful of 400s with "dimension mismatch". Customer says throughput suddenly dropped and some requests time out. sample error attached below.

infra_maya: can you paste the exact error blob and a sample request? also which model + tenant? any recent auth or quota changes? :eyes: 

support_jay: model: text-embed-large-v2, tenant: acme-enterprise-23. here's the response observed in logs: 
```
HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "error": "dimension_mismatch",
  "message": "expected dimension 1536 but got 1535 for request id req_7a2f",
  "request_id": "req_7a2f"
}
```
and also intermittent 502/504 from the embedding shard: `runtime timeout after 10s`. Some 429s too but inconsistent. No recent quota change on billing page, acme says no keys rotated.

eng_batching_lee: thanks — couple quick checks: 1) are clients sending arrays with inconsistent lengths? embedding dim mismatch is usually client-side (preprocessing) or a model variant mismatch (old model vs new). 2) tail latency + 502s suggests a batching drain issue (large request blocking batch flush/eviction). What's the current max_batch_size and dynbatch config for that model/tenant?

support_jay: pulling config now. For text-embed-large-v2 @ acme-enterprise-23: `dynamic_batching: enabled`, `max_batch_size: 64`, `max_batch_latency_ms: 30`, `batch_priority_preemption: enabled`. Also noticed a small subset of requests are much larger payloads (long documents) which correlate with the 502s.

eng_runtime_sam: aha — two likely compounding issues: (A) some clients are sending one-off long documents that produce larger-than-usual tokenization leading to odd embed vector lengths (client model mismatch or a trimming bug), (B) big requests hold the batch lock causing other small requests to wait -> tail spike. Preemptive mitigation: reduce max_batch_size to 16 for that tenant and enable partial-drain (we have a new flag) to avoid single giant request blocking the entire shard.

acme_csm: customer-side note: they pushed a pipeline change yesterday to dedupe and then run a third-party sentence-splitter. Could be related. They can roll it back if it helps.

support_jay: repro steps I captured from their SDK call: 
```
POST /v1/embeddings
Authorization: Bearer <token>
{ "model": "text-embed-large-v2", "input": ["paragraph1...","paragraph2...", "\u0000\u0000"] }
```
One client library call shows an empty string and a trailing null char; that produced a shorter embedding on our downstream side. small but real.

eng_batching_lee: yes nulls/empty strings can cause inconsistent pre-tokenization paths. For now pad/truncate inputs server-side to expected token counts and validate dims before batch commit — quick patch: reject inconsistent vectors early with a 400 and helpful message. I'll put a canary for acme.

infra_maya: I'm also seeing auth rate-limit retries for that tenant in the last 20m from multiple IPs (retry storms). Might be client SDK misconfigured retry/backoff causing thundering. We should add per-tenant retry budget and surface 429 retry-after header in SDK docs.

qa_rita: can reproduce thinly: send 1 long request + 20 tiny ones concurrently with dynbatch on max_batch_size 64 -> p99 jumps from 80ms to 3s, and one tiny request can get 502 if the long one hits kernel OOM on shard. With max_batch_size 16 it's much better (p99 ~ 250ms).

oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-2876 — Embeddings tail latency + dim_mismatch (assigned: eng-runtime).

eng_runtime_sam: action plan: 1) short-term: reduce acme tenant max_batch_size -> 16 and enable partial-drain for that shard (rolling change, low risk). 2) push server-side input validation to reject/normalize nulls/empty strings (canary to acme). 3) add a one-hour temporary per-tenant retry budget and adjust 429 handling. 4) follow up with customer to revert their sentence-splitter change and run regression tests. 5) longer-term: implement per-request size caps and backpressure counters in the batcher.

support_jay: informing customer now and scheduling a config change. Sending repro steps and suggested rollback in message. Thanks all. :pray: 

acme_csm: customer agreed to roll back splitter, and happy for the temporary max_batch_size change while they test. Please ping when deploy is scheduled.

infra_maya: scheduled rolling config update to lower max_batch_size at 2026-03-17T15:40Z (1 shard at a time). I'll monitor CPU/GPU-util and queueing.

support_jay: Update — after lowering to 16 + canary validate pad/reject logic, ACME reports p99 down to ~260ms and no more dim_mismatch errors in last 20m. Closing escalation after 1h stable window unless anything else shows up. :tada:
